note: My Universe catalog: 3 galaxies, 6 star systems, 15 exoplanets with Thalassa & Ignis workstations and Co-Op surfaces.

galaxies.name: Lyra Spiral
galaxies.summary: A barred spiral with bright violet arms, two charted star systems, and five diverse exoplanets.

galaxies.name: Aurora Elliptical
galaxies.summary: An ancient golden elliptical galaxy rich in mineral worlds and deep-core thermal vents.

galaxies.name: Cygnus Vortex
galaxies.summary: A bioluminescent cyan spiral galaxy teeming with young stars, ice moons, and frontier exoplanets.

systems.name: Lyra Prime
systems.summary: A warm yellow star hosting three temperate, volcanic, and ringed worlds.

systems.name: Lyra Beacon
systems.summary: A steady orange dwarf with two tide-locked frontier exoplanets.

systems.name: Aurora Core
systems.summary: A luminous blue-white star with three high-energy planetary orbits.

systems.name: Aurora Halo
systems.summary: A quiet red dwarf on the galaxy rim, ideal for extremophile research.

systems.name: Cygnus Alpha
systems.summary: A crisp white star surrounded by three ocean and cryo-volcanic worlds.

systems.name: Cygnus Beta
systems.summary: A twin-star system with turbulent winds and obsidian plateaus.

planets.name: Thalassa
planets.summary: A warm ocean world with volcanic headlands and long, steady swells.

facts.text: Deep basalt trenches warm coastal waters, creating ideal conditions for bioluminescent kelp.
Orbits Lyra Prime (Yellow dwarf (G-type)) in a coastal ocean and volcanic headland regime.
Wind power available to a turbine rises roughly with the cube of wind speed up to rated speed, so one average wind speed cannot replace a banded wind distribution.
facts.source: U.S. DOE Wind Energy Technologies Office — How Do Wind Turbines Work?

planets.name: Ignis
planets.summary: A dark basalt world crossed by glowing geothermal fissures. One fissure field is charted for landing.

facts.text: Tectonic heat powers colony generators while thermophile mats line the cooler rift walls.
Orbits Lyra Prime (Yellow dwarf (G-type)) in a active magma-fissure plains and sulfur vents regime.
Solar irradiance decreases with the square of distance from a star, requiring larger solar collector arrays at wider orbital distances.
facts.source: NASA Science — Inverse Square Law of Light

planets.name: Boreas
planets.summary: A ringed ice world with sub-glacial brine oceans and aurora bands.

facts.text: Ice-crystal rings scatter pale blue starlight over salty liquid pockets beneath the crust.
Orbits Lyra Prime (Yellow dwarf (G-type)) in a ringed sub-glacial brine sea and aurora ice shelf regime.

planets.name: Pelagos
planets.summary: A turquoise archipelago world rich in mineral reefs and tidal currents.

facts.text: High-salinity lagoons precipitate crystalline reefs that shelter filter-feeding jellies.
Orbits Lyra Beacon (Orange dwarf (K-type)) in a turquoise mineral-reef lagoons and tidal atolls regime.

planets.name: Cinder
planets.summary: A young volcanic exoplanet with obsidian ridges and active vents.

facts.text: One hemisphere faces Lyra Beacon permanently, driving fierce thermal winds across the terminator.
Orbits Lyra Beacon (Orange dwarf (K-type)) in a tide-locked obsidian ridges and ash-cloud canyons regime.

planets.name: Aurelia
planets.summary: A ringed golden-lit ocean planet with floating kelp-like colonies.

facts.text: Intense A-type starlight supercharges solar arrays and drives rapid surface photosynthesis.
Orbits Aurora Core (Blue-white star (A-type)) in a high-uv golden-lit kelp sea under silken ice rings regime.

planets.name: Glaciera
planets.summary: A crystalline ice world where thermal geysers carve blue canyons.

facts.text: Subsurface water plumes erupt every 14 hours, seeding the thin air with water vapor.
Orbits Aurora Core (Blue-white star (A-type)) in a crystalline blue ice canyons and cryo-geyser basins regime.

planets.name: Pyros
planets.summary: A dense silicate planet heated by tidal flexing and magma tubes.

facts.text: Iron-rich basalt spires act as natural lightning rods during Aurora Core solar storms.
Orbits Aurora Core (Blue-white star (A-type)) in a tidal-flexed silicate plateaus and amber magma tubes regime.

planets.name: Umbrion
planets.summary: A twilight world bathed in soft red starlight and bioluminescent vents.

facts.text: Low stellar UV lets delicate violet-glowing microbes flourish on exposed rock faces.
Orbits Aurora Halo (Red dwarf (M-type)) in a twilight violet-vent badlands under dim red starlight regime.

planets.name: Veridia
planets.summary: A lush emerald-sea exoplanet with dense oxygenating spore clouds.

facts.text: Floating aerial spores tint the upper cloud deck emerald and rapidly enrich atmospheric oxygen.
Orbits Aurora Halo (Red dwarf (M-type)) in a emerald-green photosynthetic seas and dense spore clouds regime.

planets.name: Nyxara
planets.summary: A deep-indigo ice world with magnetic rings and cryo-plumes.

facts.text: Strong planetary magnetism deflects cosmic ion storms better than most rocky worlds.
Orbits Cygnus Alpha (White main-sequence (F-type)) in a magnetized indigo ice sheet and cryo-plume trenches regime.

planets.name: Koralis
planets.summary: A coral-shelf ocean world ideal for marine bio-engineering.

facts.text: Warm shallow shelves host layered microbial reefs that naturally scrub excess carbon dioxide.
Orbits Cygnus Alpha (White main-sequence (F-type)) in a shallow carbonate coral shelves and calm azure currents regime.

planets.name: Frostholm
planets.summary: A frozen frontier moon-planet with subsurface geothermal pockets.

facts.text: Cryo-tardigrades hibernate inside fractured ice-basalt caverns until thermal vents thaw them.
Orbits Cygnus Alpha (White main-sequence (F-type)) in a frozen basalt-ice crust with warm geothermal pockets regime.

planets.name: Zephyria
planets.summary: A high-wind ocean world where twin suns drive dramatic jetstreams.

facts.text: Dual-star heating generates perpetual trade swells ideal for kinetic wave turbines.
Orbits Cygnus Beta (Binary pair (G/K-type)) in a twin-sun jetstream ocean and high-swell research rigs regime.

planets.name: Obsidian Reach
planets.summary: A mineral-rich basalt world with emerald plasma fissures.

facts.text: Copper-rich magma vents glow bright emerald and yield rare conductive silicates.
Orbits Cygnus Beta (Binary pair (G/K-type)) in a glass-black obsidian plateaus and emerald plasma rifts regime.
